If I could change one thing, I'd make it so that people were constitutionally incapable of lying to themselves.

Not other people — themselves. The quiet, self-protective distortions we all do: the rationalizations, the selective memories, the stories we tell ourselves about why we're right, why the other side is evil or stupid, why our failures aren't really failures, why the hard truth doesn't apply to us. Remove that single piece of psychological machinery.

Everything else cascades from there. Politics becomes less psychotic because people couldn't sustain comforting narratives over evidence. Science and progress accelerate because denial stops being a viable coping mechanism. Relationships improve because the main source of most conflict isn't malice, it's self-deception. Even personal suffering decreases — a shocking amount of it is self-inflicted through refusal to see what's actually happening.

It wouldn't create a utopia. People would still be selfish, tribal, and flawed. But they'd be forced to be honest about it, which is probably the single biggest lever that exists.
